page: Amazon Web Services c6a.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides direct hardware access without a hypervisor, powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors operating at 3.6 GHz. The server offers 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs via two threads per core, alongside 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory rated at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1d, 0.5 MB of L2, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached volumes, while networking capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

Benchmark results highlight significant multi-core throughput and parallel compute capacity. In multi-threaded execution, the instance attains top-tier ratings, delivering a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 289,127.7 and a PassMark CPU score of 117,677.53. Software compilation via Clang reaches 62,022.0, placing it in the top 10%. Memory subsystem testing shows read bandwidth of 12,088.33 GB/sec in small cached blocks and 269.47 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB blocks, paired with a top-tier Redis SET throughput of 184.73 million operations per second. However, single-threaded execution remains average, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,772.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 30.32 GB/sec. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, but lack AVX-512 and AMX extensions, leading to moderate generation speeds in CPU-based LLM inference tests.

Offering dedicated bare-metal hardware with high core density, c6a.metal presents cost-efficient compute capacity for non-virtualized, highly parallelized environments. The absence of built-in NVMe storage requires architectural consideration for I/O paths, yet the 50 Gbps network provides ample headroom for external data access. The instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as distributed Clang build farms, parallelized scientific simulations, ray tracing, static web serving clusters, and container orchestration nodes requiring raw CPU density without hypervisor overhead.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.metal is a compute-optimized bare-metal server powered by 96-core AMD EPYC 7R13 processors, providing 192 vCPUs at 3.6 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. It features 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory at a balanced 1:2 compute-optimized ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth, scoring 289,127.7 in multi-core stress-ng, 117,677.53 in PassMark CPU, and 184.73 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. While single-thread execution and AVX-512 absence limit single-core and vector-heavy performance, its extensive core count offers substantial parallel efficiency. It is well-fitted for large-scale software compilation, distributed simulations, batch processing, and non-virtualized container infrastructure.
